Hi Laura,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Attached is AceroHealth's consolidated redline to Exhibit B (pricing annex) and a short spreadsheet that runs our expected true-up under the staggered-commit scenario (see tab "Year1-Scenario"). Two items we want to confirm:

1) The "safeguard" carveout in paragraph 3(c) — we read Redwood's proposal as applying the floor only after a 90-day ramp period; we're proposing a hard-floor protection that phases in only if monthly usage drops below 45% of the committed band for two consecutive months.

2) The early-break true-up in paragraph 5 — we added an alternate calculation that caps the early-break fee to 12 months of average committed spend rather than a multiple of the then-current monthly rate.

We redlined both language and the numeric examples. We're hoping to get these resolved ahead of legal review next week. Please confirm you received the PDF.

Thanks,

Daniel —

Got the files, thanks. We've reviewed the attached PDF and the spreadsheet. Quick take:

- On the floor/safeguard: Redwood's intent for paragraph 3(c) was to provide a temporary ramp protection for the first 90 days to account for implementation variability, after which the standard floor applies unless the parties agree a written remediation plan. Acero's proposal to require a two-consecutive-month trigger at 45% is reasonable to avoid transient dips, but the language will need to preserve Redwood's ability to rely on usage telemetry and cached commitments for calculation.

- On the early-break cap: capping at 12 months of average committed spend is more client-friendly than our standard multiple. We're open to a capped remedy but need to align on the definitions ("average committed spend" vs "committed band spend") and transition mechanics.

I've looped in Karthik and Marissa — Karthik for commercial alignment and Marissa for legal redline support / alternatives that limit downside. Karthik, Marissa — can you review the attached and propose a runnable compromise? Two priorities: keep predictable unit economics for Redwood, and give Acero the operational runway they asked for.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to propose alternate numeric guardrails (45% vs 50%, 2 months vs 3 months) and show impact on ARR/true-up.
- Marissa to produce a redline that accepts a soft-floor trigger with explicit telemetry & remediation path, plus a capped early-break formula we can live with.
- We target a legal-ready redline by end of Thu 11/19.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Laura / Marissa —

Ran the numbers. Summarized options below (all assume Acero's baseline commit is Band B: 150M tokens/month):

Option A — Client-friendly (Acero proposal-ish):
- Trigger: 45% of committed band for 2 consecutive months
- Floor application: Soft-floor for first 6 months (no billing correction) then hard-floor thereafter
- Early-break cap: 12 months of average committed spend
- Revenue impact (pro-forma year 1): ~ -7% net vs baseline

Option B — Balanced (compromise):
- Trigger: 50% for 3 consecutive months
- Floor application: 90-day ramp + 3-month remediation window before floor enforcement
- Early-break cap: 9 months of committed band spend
- Revenue impact: ~ -3%

Option C — Redwood-preferred:
- Trigger: 55% for 3 months
- Floor: immediate after 90-day ramp
- Early-break cap: 12 months of committed band spend plus surcharge multiplier for usage decline >70%
- Revenue impact: ~ +2%

My recommendation: Option B. It preserves predictability while giving Acero runway. Laura, if you want, I can produce a one-page summary to send to Acero's CFO (Lydia) showing annual true-up under the three options for transparency.

Karthik

Laura / Karthik —

Attached is a proposed redline that attempts to bridge Acero's ask and Redwood's need for clear measurement. Key points in the redline:

- Defined "Committed Band Spend" as the product of the committed token band and Redwood's published unit price for that band, with telemetry defined as the canonical source (API keys + account_id).
- Trigger clause: accept 50% threshold for 3 consecutive months (Option B) with a documented remediation plan window of 60 days post-trigger before floor enforcement; this prevents knee-jerk billing corrections and gives both parties a playbook.
- Early-termination cap: propose 9 months of Committed Band Spend plus a fixed taper for any months where formal remediation is underway (reduces cliff impact).
- Added a short carveout allowing Redwood to apply a temporary rollback of discounts if usage permanently shifts downward by >60% for 6+ months, but only after customer notice and a 30-day cure period.

I've embedded inline comments where Acero's prior language (two-month trigger at 45%) creates operational ambiguity. If we align on Option B / Marissa redline, I think legal-to-legal review will clear quickly.

I'll produce a clean PDF redline for legal to exchange and a one-page impact summary for Lydia. Laura, want me to send the PDF to Daniel directly or should we route via you?

-Marissa
